newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - U.S. blue chips lift Euro-stocks off lows.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. blue chips lift Euro-stocks off lows.

text.p: European stocks pulled off session lows in afternoon European trading on Thursday after U.S. blue chips reversed an opening loss of about 30 points made after the dollar went into sharp decline against the yen overnight.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average recovered from the weaker dollar, government bond weakness and an early bout of profit-taking after Wednesday's surge to a record close with help from the Nasdaq index.
The Nasdaq, comprised mostly of small-capitalisation and technology stocks, got a lift into positive ground from strong fourth-quarter earnings predictions from Intel Corp.
Wall Street's recovery helped European stocks pare losses, made early on after the dollar's steep fall and weaker government bond prices.

The dollar started sliding in Tokyo after a Japanese finance ministry official said the currency's recovery from last year's post-war low against the yen was nearly complete and that Japan's economy was stronger than the markets believed.
"Bonds and the dollar have led us down across the board," said one London trader.
The dollar remained under pressure after the head of the National Association of Manufacturers said the Clinton administration was likely to de-emphasize a strong dollar policy.
By 1600 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.5083 marks and 111.50 yen, compared with 1.5165 marks and 113.83 yen in late European trade on Wednesday.
But traders said the dollar remained vulnerable as worldwide interest rate jitters continued to rattle stock and bond markets.

"The initial signal did not come from the new U.S. administration as many expected but from Japan, where it appears the groundwork is being laid for a rate hike," said Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"The Japanese are trying to put a 115 yen top in," said Stephen Flanagan, a vice president at Credit Agricole in the U.S. "You've probably got more downside as all these yen-financed bond trades around the world are put at risk."
In Paris, the blue-chip CAC-40 moved back above 2,200, lingering just below steady levels, after being as low as 2,194.17 earlier in the day.

British shares also trimmed losses after falling below 3,900 earlier but remained unnerved by Wednesday's Bank of England forecast of an imminent rise in inflation and the probable need for higher interest rates.

Some traders also noted pressure on the London's blue-chip FTSE-100 index coming from derivatives-related selling, including an options trade worth $1.6 billion that is betting on the market falling sharply by next June.
The German DAX index ended floor dealings lower, dragged down by a sharp fall in the shares of German electronic firm Siemens, which had already tumbled in Wednesday's post-bourse electronic trade.
The dollar's weakness, bad for German exporters, also pressured the market and overshadowed an overnight record close on Wall Street.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5083 marks and 111.50 yen, compared with 1.5165 marks and 113.83 yen in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1600 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 35.4 points lower at 3,900.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 1.56 at 2,211.81
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index fell 15.97 at 2,713.22.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1600 GMT
Afternoon gold fixed at $378.60 against $378.00 previously, helped by buying in New York after declines in stocks, bonds and the dollar. Silver was down unchanged from the previous close at $4.78.
